_comment: Per-repo configuration for the portfolio CI/CD floor - see CICD_FLOOR.md. The floor's workflows and scripts are byte-identical in every repo; everything that legitimately differs between repos lives here instead, so a repo can change its own settings without regenerating anything and the installer's copies stay verifiably identical. A pull request CAN weaken its own checks by editing this file, which is why changes to it want the same review attention as a change to a workflow - the floor-drift check is what catches divergence that nobody approved. Every key here is read by something today: codeqlLanguages, testCommand and docsCheck were removed because nothing read them - they were written ahead of the code that would, the same way scheduledScriptDir was, and a key nobody reads is a key that eventually gets trusted wrongly. CICD_FLOOR.md still documents the design for each; add the key back in the change that adds the reader.

knownAbsentPaths..github/workflows/call-hub.yml: a SPOKE's file, not the hub's - this repo documents it extensively because managing spokes is its whole job, and setup_spoke.py generates it. Cited on ~7 README lines and will keep growing, which is why this belongs here rather than as per-line markers.
knownAbsentPaths.gas/.clasp.json: gitignored by design - it carries a scriptId tied to one person's Google account. gas/.clasp.json.example is the checked-in template, and that one does resolve.
knownAbsentPaths.meta/FLOW_DOCTRINE.md: a KOS file, cited for attribution where this repo's queue-liveness checks were ported from. Attributed as KOS's in the surrounding prose.

optionalSecrets.AI_API_KEY: normally lives only as a Vercel env var, not an Actions secret - an Actions runner cannot read Vercel's env either way, so its absence here is expected unless it has been deliberately mirrored. doctor.js's own AI check degrades to a clean skip for the same reason.
optionalSecrets.AI_BASE_URL: same as AI_API_KEY - a Vercel env var, mirrored to Actions only if someone chose to.
optionalSecrets.CLASPRC_JSON: deploy-apps-script.yml gates every step that uses this behind its "Check required secrets are configured" step, which reports a clean skip when CLASPRC_JSON/GAS_SCRIPT_ID are unset - the floor's "graceful degradation, not perpetual red" convention. Absent until a real Apps Script deployment exists, and harmless until then.
optionalSecrets.GAS_PROD_DEPLOYMENT_ID: deploy-apps-script.yml gates every step that uses this behind its "Check required secrets are configured" step, which reports a clean skip when CLASPRC_JSON/GAS_SCRIPT_ID are unset - the floor's "graceful degradation, not perpetual red" convention. Absent until a real Apps Script deployment exists, and harmless until then.
optionalSecrets.GAS_SCRIPT_ID: deploy-apps-script.yml gates every step that uses this behind its "Check required secrets are configured" step, which reports a clean skip when CLASPRC_JSON/GAS_SCRIPT_ID are unset - the floor's "graceful degradation, not perpetual red" convention. Absent until a real Apps Script deployment exists, and harmless until then.
optionalSecrets.GAS_STAGING_DEPLOYMENT_ID: deploy-apps-script.yml treats the staging deployment as optional and reports a clean skip without it - see that workflow's secrets gate.
optionalSecrets.GAS_STAGING_WEB_APP_URL: same as GAS_STAGING_DEPLOYMENT_ID - only needed once a staging deployment exists.

Absent until a real Apps Script deployment exists, and harmless until then.
